descriptions.text: Incorrect Token Burn Mechanism. Lost: 150.2 WBNB

EST's BNBDeposit staking contract tracks accounting using the EST/WBNB PancakeSwap pair's reserves and balances, but the EST token's transfer/burn mechanism lets the pair's real EST balance be manipulated relative to its accounted reserves. Using a 20,000 WBNB flash loan from Moolah, the attacker (an EOA that delegated code via EIP-7702 because the deposit contract only allows EOAs to claim) deposited the maximum repeatedly, bought EST, then sent 1 EST to the deposit contract to desync its internal state. The core exploit was a 100-iteration loop that transferred EST into the pair and called skim() to the deposit contract: skim pushes out the excess (un-reserved) token balance, and because of EST's flawed burn/fee mechanics this repeatedly inflated the deposit contract's credited balance. The attacker then swapped all the harvested EST back to WBNB, repaid the flash loan, and netted ~150.2 WBNB.
